To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a PTH-r-P derived peptide, designated PTR4, capable of binding HLA-A2 molecules was identified; b) PTR4 was able to induce a CTL response against PTH-r-P+ cells, including autologous prostate cancer metastases in vitro; and c) PTR4 peptide-pulsing autologous DC was capable of breaking the tolerance against autologous prostate tumour by inducing PTH-r-P specific CTL immune reaction.
we have developed a novel strategy of generating PTH-rP- specific CTL lines in vitro, using autologous tumours and PTR-4-peptides pulsed dendritic cells.

PTR-4, a PTH-rp-specific peptide is capable to bind the HLA-A2 molecule, to generate a PTH-r-rp-specific CTL response and to induce the generation of an in vitro efficient PTH-r-r-p-specific CTL response by cyclostimulation of TIL with PTR-4 peptide-loaded autologoues DC and low-dose of IL-2, in a patient with metastasic prostrate carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the PTH-rP epitope recognized by the CTL and with the possibility of generating a specific CTL response in vivo.
the generation of a CTL response against a peptide derived from PTH-rP.
the development of a new immunotherapy for prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper provides evidence for the induction of PTH-rP- specific CTL immune reaction by in vitro stimulation with PTR-4 peptide-loaded autologou s dendritic cells and IL-2.
the results presented here provide a proof of principle that the use of PTR-4 peptide loaded autologous DC can be an efficient strategy for the induction of a PTH-rp specific CTL response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PTHrP peptide-pulsed dendritic cells were able to induce a CTL response in prostate cancer patients, which could be used in adoptive immunotherapy.
we were the first to show that a peptide from PTH-rP could induce CTLs in vitro, and that this peptide could be used to induce PTH-rP CTLs from TILs.
the use of autologous dendritics cell pulsed with a peptide of PTH-rP (PTH-rP-4) was able to break tolerance of TIL against autologous tumours by inducing a specific CTL immune reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have identified a peptide from the parathyroid-homone-related protein (PTH-rP), which has been shown to play a major role in the pathogenesis of prostate cancer, and we have shown that this peptide can stimulate the immune system to kill prostate cancer cells.

we can generate an effective PTH-rP peptide-specific T-cell response by in vitro stimulation with PTR-4 peptide-loaded autologus dendritic cells (aDC) of tumour-inflitrating lymphocytes (aTIL) from a patient with hormone-resistant metastatic prostate cancer.
the PTH-rP peptide can be used to generate CTLs that can be adoptively transferred to patients with metastatic prostate cancer to treat their bone metastases.
